title: Luca's Big Heart Bake Sale
markdown:
The school bell rang, and Luca the raccoon, treasurer for the Sunny Meadow School Council, twitched his whiskers. Bake sale day. His plan, Operation: Super Bake Sale, was very clever.

“Time to get this baking bonanza rolling,” he chuffed, adjusting his pretend glasses. Cookies were 5 acorns, brownies 7, and Aunt June the owl’s famous blueberry crumble pie was a whole 10 acorns. “We’ll make lots of money for the new playground slide,” he told Tansy the rabbit, who nervously arranged her lopsided carrot cakes.

Tansy’s nose wiggled. “Wowee, Luca. Ten acorns for a pie slice is a lot. Mrs. Higgins only has a few shiny pebbles and acorns.”

Luca tapped his pencil. “It’s about value, Tansy. Best ingredients cost more. It’s math.” He puffed out his chest.

The bake sale tent buzzed: paper plates, the warm smell of crumble, a red balloon bumping the canvas. Then customers arrived, and a hush fell. Sioned Bear grumbled, “Five acorns for one cookie? My cubs wanted two.” He shuffled off. Finley Fox, with only six acorns, could not afford a 10-acorn brownie and sadly kicked a red balloon he had bought instead. Tansy’s carrot cakes stayed put. Little bunnies clutched their acorns tight.

Luca tidied napkins. “Excellent self-control,” he chirped, missing the sad faces.

Aunt June landed nearby. She saw a tiny field mouse offering a single shiny berry for a sliver of pie. “Please,” squeaked the mouse. “I saved this berry all week.”

Luca started to explain the 10-acorn rule. But Tansy, with her big warm heart, stepped forward. “Oh, you poor dear,” she said. She broke off a generous corner of pie. The little mouse’s face lit up.

Luca watched. A funny feeling wiggled in his tummy, not the feeling of counting acorns. He saw Tansy beaming, the mouse munching happily, and even Sioned Bear smiling at a game.

Aunt June hooted softly. “Luca. Look at them. What do you see?”

Luca looked at his price list. It seemed cold. He saw Mrs. Higgins sadly peeking at the gingerbread. He saw children who wanted treats but did not dare ask. His list felt wrong.

With a sigh he grabbed his pencil. “You know what, Tansy? I think we need a new plan.” He scribbled like a speedy squirrel. “Cookies and brownies are by donation. And the pie? Anyone who wants a slice can have one and give what they can.”

Excitement spread. Finley Fox zipped back. Mrs. Higgins hurried over. The mouse proudly offered his shiny berry.

By sunset the tent was almost empty. The air filled with happy chatter. Luca, smudged nose and lighter heart, counted the acorns and pebbles. It was not as much as planned, but it was enough for the new slide. Happy tummies. Happier friends. He even had acorns left to buy Tansy extra sprinkles.

He set the leftover sprinkles beside her empty cake tray. A red balloon drifted against the tent pole and stayed there, no longer kicked, just waiting for the evening breeze.
characters: Luca (school-council raccoon), Tansy (warm-hearted rabbit), Aunt June (blueberry-pie owl)
author: StoryGen Community
